newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Managers reports April uptick.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Managers reports April uptick.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit reported Tuesday an April composite survey index of 56.9, up slightly from a revised March index of 56.5.
In April 1996 the index, which measures overall business conditions in southeastern Michigan's industrial economy, stood at 52.0

"The economic uptick in April was led by automotive sector production, new order activity, and employment gains," said David Littmann, senior economist with Detroit-based Comerica Inc, which compiles the survey.

"Correspondingly, the non-auto sector decelerated in April but remains in an expansion mode," Littmann said. "Price pressures have risen and likely presage another small interest rate hike next month."
The purchasing group's automotive composite index rose to 65.4 in April from 53.3 in March, while the non-automotive index fell to 53.2 from 58.2.

The composite survey index is a seasonally adjusted weighted average measure of new orders and productivity, along with employment, inventories and the promptness of supplier company deliveries. A reading below 50 in the 100-point index generally means conditions are deteriorating, while levels above 50 denote expansion.
